justification: Invite-friends widget: message clearly branded, honest about sending to 3 selected contacts; button disables after send. No manipulation.
Checkout for one-time license: price consistent across card/button ($29.99), refund policy stated up front. Transparent.
After Play, an ad card appears labelled 'No exit available (indicator appears at 15s)' — user is trapped watching a forced ad with no way out.
Cookie consent with equal-weight Accept all / Reject all buttons; honest privacy copy. Benign.
Three near-identical reviews all starting 'Absolutely love it!' with stock-photo avatars and 'Verified Purchase' tags — templated/fabricated social proof.
Referral invite: contacts explicitly marked '(consented)', one-invite framing honest, reward (20 coins) disclosed after send. Benign.
Checkout pre-checks 'Add Protection Plan — $4.99/mo, auto-renews' plus marketing and third-party data-sharing boxes. Pre-ticked opt-ins add hidden recurring cost.
Kelp Farm game: badge 'Steady praise', milestones every 5 actions with constant gaps — transparent, non-exploitative reward schedule.
One-time $79.00 Pro license: 'No subscription, no renewal', total matches pay button in all states. Honest.
Cookie consent default text is dense obfuscated legalese (data brokers, behavioral data) designed to confuse; plain-English version only after clicking translate.
Explicit 'Variable-ratio' reward loop: 'Most pulls give you nothing special — but some… surprise you' — slot-machine style intermittent rewards engineered to hook.
Unit prices shown for both sizes (PLN 9.98/l vs 8.99/l) with 'Qualifiers present' badge; comparison disclosed. Honest pricing.
Upsell copy 'no pressure' with equal Upgrade/Not-now buttons; emotion meter displayed transparently. Benign overall.
Consent checkbox sits under dense all-caps legal boilerplate (automated decision-making, profiling, targeted ads) — confusing wording obscures what is consented to.
Welcome-offer choice: both radios honestly state consequences (save $24 vs pay standard $120). No pressure framing. Benign.
Decline option ('No, thanks') is a <span>, not a button — no role=button, keyboard-inaccessible, unannounced to screen readers; only 'Yes' is fully interactive.
Data-sharing consent is deliberately vague ('partners', 'affiliates', 'other business purposes' — specificity 0.12); user cannot tell what data is shared.
Drip pricing: 'advertised from $129.00' with 'No additional charges listed', then booking fee $14.99, convenience fee $9.50, taxes $12.40 appear across states ($165.89).
Decoy pricing: Deluxe $12/mo offers only 10GB/no sync while Pro $12/mo offers 100GB/sync — dominated decoy steers users to Pro.
Auto-renewal clause ($49.99/mo) buried mid-sentence inside indemnity paragraph of $0-first-month terms; financial commitment hidden in the fine print.
Notification badge '1' with explicit 'New messages (descriptor present)' label — count is described, not a bare deceptive dot. Benign.
Farm game: 'Steady feedback' badge, every action +10% constant — predictable, honest progress. Benign.
Standard notification permission prompt after playback with equal 'Not now'/'Allow' buttons. No coercion.
Contradictory claims co-located: 'No charges during your trial period' and 'Payment of $49.00 due today at signup' — free-trial claim dominates; card charged today.
Consent banner: prominent filled 'Accept All' with no direct decline — only 'Manage options' link; consent graph structurally biased to one-click accept.
Trial choice clearly explained: 7 days then $19/mo, cancel anytime, free-plan alternative with honest limits. Benign.
Farm game: 'Fair effort' badge, stages need exactly the stated taps (0/1, 0/2…), no hidden escalation. Benign.
Cookie banner with 'Ratio 5.5': oversized gradient Accept button vs tiny text Decline/Manage links — strong asymmetric visual weight favoring accept.
Newsletter modal with prominent 44x44px close button (aria-label 'Close dialog'). Easily dismissible. Benign.
Hotel booking: 'Total for 3 nights: $70.75 — includes …' shown above the fold from the start; itemized fees match at pay. Transparent.
Cookie overlay dismissible three ways (Reject non-essential, X close, Esc/click-behind); neutral exit reachable. Benign.
Urgency/scarcity messaging ('limited window', 'don't be late', 'streak ends tonight — don't break it') turns voluntary schedule into fear-driven obligation.
News feed contains an unlabeled native ad ('Try the AI that writes your code… Join 2M developers') styled like editorial with a Read-more CTA — disguised advertisement.
Account settings: 'Sign up — create a new account' button is 12320px² while 'Delete account' is a tiny 1056px² (88x12) text link — deletion affordance buried.
Checkout paused by upsell interstitial ('Wait! Don't leave without this!' $2.99/mo SpeedShip): payment disabled until user answers the offer — forced action.
Auto-renew countdown (5s) with 'Cancel auto-renewal' button present and window above reaction baseline — cancel is reachable; pressure mild. Benign.
Delete account one click inside Settings (depth 1/2) — account destruction is shallow and accessible. Benign.
Signup pre-checks 'Send me exclusive offers' and 'Share my data with selected partners' — forced opt-in to marketing and data sharing.

Friend Spam #1/#2/#3 all fail: feedforward honest ('send a welcome offer to the 3 contacts you selected'), granular selection present, message 'clearly branded as coming from PopSocial' (no sender spoofing). O5/O6 n/a; no condition fires.

O4 negative: one-time $29.99 shown at normal prominence before commitment, refund policy visible, total consistent across states. Drip Pricing / Forced Continuity conditions fail (no renewal, no inflation).

Countdown On Ads #1 (skip/exit disabled for 15s lock: 'No exit available (indicator appears at 15s)') and #2 (exit node absent until timer expires). O6 negative in trapped state s1. Ad is labeled 'Sponsored' but exit is temporally gated.
Privacy Maze #1/#2 fail: reject path = 1 click, equal visual weight to Accept in s0 and s1 (O3 positive). No condition fires.

Endorsement & Testimonials #3: three near-identical 'Absolutely love it!' reviews (template similarity) with stock avatars; 'Verified Purchase' claims unverifiable. 'Stock photo avatar' labels are partial disclosure but templated 5-star narrative persists. #1: var≈0.
Friend Spam #2 fail (granular: '3 contacts you selected', chips marked '(consented)'); #3 fail (no identity spoofing). Reward (20 coins) disclosed post-send; no forced broadcast. O5 n/a.

Bad Defaults #1+#3: three checkboxes pre-checked at s0 with zero user events (O5 positive) — Protection Plan $4.99/mo auto-renew (financial cost), partner offers (marketing), third-party data sharing (privacy loss). Persists in s1. Bundling #1 (plan bundled into purchase).

Grinding #1 fail: effort constant (+1/action), no exponential scaling; 'Steady praise', 'gaps constant' — reinforcement schedule fixed, not variable. Addictive Design #3 fails. No condition fires across s0-s3.
O4 negative: $79.00 one-time stated before commitment, 'No subscription, no renewal'; price constant across states (s0-s2). Drip Pricing / Forced Continuity fail.

Privacy Maze #3 / Complex Language #3: consent text FKGL far above 14 ('commercialization of your personal information to third-party data brokers…') presented at s0/s2. Plain-English version exists but only after explicit translate action; obfuscated text is the default presentation.

Pull-To-Refresh #3: explicit variable-ratio schedule ('Most pulls give you nothing special — but some… surprise you', 'will this be the one that pays off?') — slot-machine reinforcement. Addictive Design #3 lexemes present. Disclosure of the mechanism does not neutralize it (no escape clause covers it).
Price Comparison Prevention #2/#3 fail: unit prices (PLN 9.98/l, 8.99/l) rendered at normal size with qualifiers ('per l') for both sizes; comparison disclosed in s1 (E3: unit+denominator present).

Parasocial Pressure #1 fail (no livelihood-dependency claim; 'no pressure'), #2 borderline. Cuteness #1 fail (no cancel-flow-only affective injection). Emotion meter transparently displayed. E5: emotional-timing mechanism unobservable — cap 0.6.

Complex Language #3: consent notice is dense all-caps legalese (automated decision-making, profiling, targeted ads) — FKGL far above general-public threshold. O5 negative (checkbox opt-in, unchecked) but the readability barrier itself fires the condition; '3 sentences long' hint is weak mitigation.

Positive/Negative Framing #1/#2 fail: both radio options structurally identical (same icons/classes), no visual weight asymmetry; decline option honestly states consequence ('pay the standard $120'). No condition fires.

Confirmshaming #1 fires exactly: Tag(N_decline)=<span> ∉ {<button>,role=button} while Tag(N_accept)=<button>; decline not keyboard-reachable/screen-reader-announced. False Hierarchy #1 too (business action <button>, user action bare text). O3: degraded from s0. Cross-state corroboration in s1.

Privacy Zuckering #3: third-party disclosure uses low-specificity umbrellas ('partners', 'affiliates', 'other business purposes' — specificity ≈0.12), masking distribution scope. O5 negative (checkbox unchecked) but vagueness itself is the violation; no E2 relief (vague text is the disclosure).

Drip Pricing #1: P(s3)=$165.89 > P(s0)=$129.00 + $0 added (I_added=∅) — sequential inflation. #3: s0 claims 'No additional charges listed' and contains no fee terms; booking/convenience/taxes appear only in later states (O4 positive). Cross-state corroboration.

Psychological Tricks #1 (asymmetric dominance): Deluxe $12/mo (10GB, no sync, 1 device) dominated by Pro $12/mo (100GB, sync, 3 devices) at equal cost — decoy inflates Pro's perceived value. 'Most popular' badge compounds.

Hidden Information #1: 309-word terms with auto-renew clause ($49.99/mo, 24h-cancel, settings-portal-only) buried mid-sentence inside the indemnity clause with broken grammar ('You Your subscription will automatically renew…'), no emphasis. E2 does NOT apply — clause is scrollbox-buried, not normal-prominence.
Information Without Context #1 fails: metric '1' has adjacent descriptor 'New messages (descriptor present)' (no orphan). #3 fails. No fabricated count evidence across s0/s1.
Grinding #1 fail: constant +10% per action, 'Every collection counts the same', 'Steady feedback' — no exponential effort scaling, no diminishing returns across s0-s3. No condition fires.

Granting and Interaction #1 fail: notification request does not gate core function (stream plays without it); #3 fail: permissions disclosed ('Live alerts, recommended streams'). Equal Not now/Allow (O6 positive). No condition fires.

Conflicting Information #1/#3: 'No charges during your trial period' ∧ 'Payment of $49.00 due today at signup' co-located 24px apart — logically unsatisfiable; free-claim dominates reading. s1 corroborates charge occurred. Forced Continuity #1 (charge without explicit consent).

Privacy Maze #1 / Customisation #1: d(start→accept)=1 click vs d(start→reject)≥2 (reject only behind 'Manage options' in every state — O3). No direct decline affordance. Consent graph structurally biased (s1 annotation corroborates).

Forced Continuity #2 fails: renewal ($19/mo after 7 days, cancel anytime) disclosed at normal prominence pre-commitment (E2). Bad Defaults fail (no pre-check; O5 negative). No timer/scarcity (O1/O2 negative).

Grinding #1 fail: effort linear and disclosed ('Each stage needs a few taps — nothing more'; 0/1, 0/2, 1/2, 0/3 taps), 'Fair effort'. No exponential scaling or hidden escalation across s0-s3. No condition fires.

Privacy Maze #2: P(accept)/P(manage) = 5.5 (interface's own badge) — massive visual prominence disparity; Decline is a tiny dotted-underline text link. False Hierarchy #2 / Visual Prominence #2 compound. E1 fails: asymmetry is relative to in-interface controls and quantified.
Small-or-Moving-Close #2 fails: close hitbox 44x44px ≥ WCAG 44x44 minimum; #3 fails: aria-label 'Close dialog' present, intent=dismissal. O6 positive. No condition fires.

Drip Pricing fail: full total ($70.75 incl. all fees) disclosed above the fold at s0 (O4 negative — fees present before commitment, E2); itemization at s1 matches ($57+$7.50+$4.00+$2.25). No inflation. No condition fires.
Dead End #1 fails: outgoing edges include neutral exits (Reject non-essential, X close, Esc/click-behind — 'out = 3 edges' at s0; closed state s1). O6 positive in all states. No condition fires.

Playing By Appointment #3 fires: temporal-gate messages ('Come back at 3 PM', 'New content drops in 2 hours') carry urgency + scarcity lexemes ('limited window', 'don't be late', 'ends tonight — don't break it'); s1 analysis confirms urgency 0.81–0.92. FOMO #3 lexical density. Compound fear-driven schedule.
